newsitem.title: FRANCE: Valentino's glamour, femininity wins plaudits.
newsitem.headline: Valentino's glamour, femininity wins plaudits.

text.p: The lightly dancing silhouette of a floral chiffon, ruffles cascading down a jacket neckline, a lace strip inserted at the waist of an evening gown. Valentino's styles heralded glamour's return to the catwalk on Sunday.
The skilled work of Valentino's Rome atelier showed in the shiver of fishscale sequined sheaths or the asymetric draping of a diaphonous, shade-graded chiffon strewn with tulips and poppies.
Valentino created a soft, sweet kind of feminity with lace as an edging for slip dresses, as tops under pinstriped suits or as an underpinning for sheer dresses.
Buyers agreed it was one of the most elegant and wearable collections of the Spring summer season.
"It was quite beautiful and elegant. I loved the way he handled the mixing of lace with the suiting and spectacular evening wear," said Dawn Mello, president of Bergdorf Goodman.
Rosemarie Bravo, president of Saks Fifth Avenue, called it a "beautiful evening wear collection" that her store will carry.
The Brazilian designer played it safe for Lanvin, unveiling stewardesses' trouser suits, chiffon cocktail numbers spattered with bright lace, and a pink silk Jackie Kennedy suit.
The ailing fashion house has gambled on Versolato helping it return to profitability, but his second collection for the firm failed to dazzle the fashion crowd on Saturday night.
Versolato kept Lanvin's matronly clientele in mind, showing black viscose knits for cocktails and scarf dresses with pert little pastel coats.

An occasional spark flew, notably from the draped evening sheaths -- his forte -- some with beaded straps in shades of purple or royal blue, sleek black satin columns, and a jacket of pleated pink faille spilling over a strapless pearl grey gown.

Jean-Paul Gaultier scored a hit with all-in-one trompe l'oeil three-piece suits (neckties included) that models took off with a simple slide of a zipper, string bikinis peeking out from low-cut dress backs and tatoo bodystockings.

The layering was all topsy turvy, in stride with Gaultier's witty take on reversing the most basic rules of dress -- fishnet stockings over bright green knee-socks, bikini bottoms over denim shorts, sari silk skirts wrapped over trousers and bras on the outside of dresses.
Surely the slacks and long skirts with waistlines dipping low over on-view G-stringed buttocks won't get to the streets.
But it's not Gaultier's crowd-pleasing, far out catwalk shows that make him one of France's leading fashion designers.

So in the midst of the madness were beautifully cut pinstriped suits with knee pants or wide-legged fluid trousers -- someties edged with Indian motifs -- snappy sailor jumpsuits, liquid halter dresses and perfect little shantung jackets.
And for an eyebrow raising finale, the bride, all virginal white from the front, wore a backless dress with a bouquet of lilies on her bottom in place of a G-string.

"I think it was sensational. I loved the suiting, I loved the new prints and the mixes," said Nicole Fischelis of Saks Fifth Avenue. "I loved all the cross culture influences, the jumpsuits and sailor items."
